item.content:encoded: Echoing the sentiments of a lot of others in this thread, it’s simply boring, which is a shame. I had a physical “wait a minute” moment when I made the connection with magnet disruptions and Bermuda, and I was like “OK, I’m ready for something super weird and cool like SCP-1000”. Instead, it’s just… a cloud that eats thing, we don’t even know how it does it. Like what Roget said, more detail would do this good, and perhaps a more interesting base for the anomaly? As of now, it gets the downvote.

item.content:encoded:
The idea definitely has potential but the article doesn't do it justice. If there were perhaps some different context or presentation it would be better, because as it stands it's a pretty straight urban legend/myth transition of the bermuda triangle in the SCP format. I'm not saying it needs to have a tweest, just to put some kind of more fresh spin than the straightforward way this is presented.

I also feel like more detail about the feeding phenomenon and how its active state behaves would do the article a lot of good. Those are the areas the article should be getting its meat from but they seemed skimmed over. This contributes to it being a more or less straightforward transition of the bermuda triangle.

Also, the addendum doesn't add anything.

item.content:encoded:
It has taken me quite a while to decide whether to downvote this article on top of expressing my opinion or let it be. In the end I've chosen the former, that said I like the concept and I'm sure it could be improved.

Anyway, what I do not like about this article:
- it obviously refers to the Bermuda Triangle yet blanks out the name
- it refers to a real-life (or as close as it can get to it, considering we're talking about the Triangle here) event/phenomenon, which I personally do not like
- it reads as if the Foundation had pretty much given up on studying this SCP
- it tells us about all those difficulties, uncontainability being of course one of the major ones - and just expects us to believe in them
- what is "semi-active state" anyway?

item.content:encoded:
Scorecard of Bermuda Triangle explanations:

  • Seafloor methane gas pockets: meh
  • Aliens: A bigger cliche than radiation creating superpowers
  • Potentially sentient weather system that eats planes and ships: YES

Indisputable winner: SCP-605.

Edit @ Unimport: Yes. Yes we do. (Within reason. Like the test of SCP-698 on 682 being the cause of the LHC breaking is an example of Doing It Right, while "poking a globe that affects the earth caused Hurricane Katrina" is definitely Doing It Wrong, not to mention #19 in the cliche list.)
